messages.subject: Problems regarding vegetation indices values
messages.body_plain:
Hello Filipe. I hope you are doing well.

I have questions regarding some vegetation index values.
I have been using a shapefile to extract spectral information from an orthomosaic. The spectral bands are extracted perfectly, but I have been having problems with the values of the VIs. The values of the VIs are not reliable. For example, when I use band values to calculate the VIs in Excel, these values are different from those generated directly by the package. The VI that had the most discrepant values was the VARI.
Would you know what could be happening?

I look forward to hearing from you soon.

Best regards

messages.subject: Re: Problems regarding vegetation indices values
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Thanks for contacting us...!

The package applies the index equation in the entire image pixel
by pixel. This allows to evaluate all variation in the plot. When you extract
the single band average per plot to calculate index using EXCEL, the equation
will be applied only once accounting only the plot average. This can input some
bias to the final value (ex: plots with more soil exposed – you will reduce the
greenness average compared to the values calculated pixel by pixel in the
package). Also, that´s why you do not see difference for single bands values (average
will be the same) but is seeing for indices values.

Hope it makes sense...!

All the best,

Filipe

messages.subject: Problemas com o corte para estimar a altura
messages.subject_clean: Problemas com o corte para estimar a altura
messages.body_plain:
Boa tarde,

Estou tendo problemas para realizar o corte de imagem utilizando o comando fieldShape.
Eu uso o comando:
DSM0.C <- fieldCrop(mosaic = DSM0,fieldShape = EX1.Crop)
E recebo a mensagem:
Error in if (projection(fieldShape) != projection(mosaic)) { :
  valor ausente onde TRUE/FALSE necessário.

Eu tentei seguir pra próxima fase de estimar a altura realizando o corte de maneira "manual", mas isso faz com que no momento que é necessário a remoção do solo com a mascara que é utilizada, não tenha sobreposição da imagem. Dessa forma, aparece o erro:
Error in .local(x, y, ...) : extents do not overlap

Aguardo o retorno.
Att, Julia Teixeira.

messages.body_plain:
Boa Tarde Julia,

Provavelmente seu DSM0 e EX1.Crop (1) não estão na mesma localidade, (2) não possuem a mesma projeção, (3) seu EX1.Crop é maior que o DSM0 e no momento do corte algumas partes com NA estão sendo capturados, (4) etc. Tem muitas possíveis explicações... Só vendo os exemplos pra saber.

Tenta rodar assim:

projection(EX1.Crop) <- projection(DSM0)

DSM0.C <- fieldCrop(mosaic = DSM0,fieldShape = EX1.Crop)

Vê se funciona. Caso não, seria interessante compartilhar o exemplo...!

Obrigado,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: fieldDraw tool
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marcelo,

 Thanks for asking... I am not sure if I know how to answer your question.

 Did you try saving the output "$drawObject" as a shapefile with writeOGR?

 Another possibility is to save the $drawData$x and $drawData$y. In this case, you do not need to draw lines again... Also, you can use this information to create a SpatialLinesDataFrame and save it.

 Let us know if it helps...!

 All the best,

Filipe
